title: Auth Token Lifecycle
purpose: Full JWT token lifecycle from Supabase Auth creation through storage (localStorage/sessionStorage), transmission (Bearer header), verification (supabase.auth.getUser), expiry (401 → auto-clear), and logout (clear storage + supabase.auth.signOut). Show the refresh token gap (no rotation implemented).
description: Seven-stage JWT lifecycle for the PoDM platform: (1) Creation via supabase.auth.signInWithPassword returning access_token + refresh_token. (2) Client-side storage in localStorage or sessionStorage based on Remember Me preference via useAuth.tsx. (3) Transmission on every API request via apiClient.ts interceptor attaching Authorization: Bearer header. (4) Server-side verification via supabase.auth.getUser(token) remote API call—no local JWT decode. (5) Session continuation: verified token reused for subsequent requests until expiry. (6) Expiry handling: 401 response intercepted by apiClient.ts response interceptor—clears token from storage, redirects to login. (7) Logout: supabase.auth.signOut() clears storage and redirects. Key gaps highlighted: no refresh token rotation (user logged out mid-session), no silent refresh mechanism, localStorage XSS vulnerability (plaintext token).

actors.label: Frontend (React)
actors.description: React SPA managing token storage via useAuth.tsx, token attachment via apiClient.ts, and token lifecycle events.

modules.label: Supabase Auth
modules.description: JWT issuer and validator. Creates tokens on sign-in, validates via supabase.auth.getUser(). Server-side client: autoRefreshToken=false, persistSession=false.

modules.label: Auth Middleware (auth.middleware.ts)
modules.description: Validates JWT on every authenticated request via remote Supabase API call.

modules.label: apiClient.ts (Axios interceptors)
modules.description: HTTP client with request interceptor (attach token) and response interceptor (handle 401 → clear → redirect).

modules.label: useAuth.tsx
modules.description: React hook managing token state in React context and browser storage. Handles login and logout.

dataStores.label: localStorage / sessionStorage
dataStores.description: Browser storage for JWT tokens. localStorage for persistent sessions, sessionStorage for session-only. Both are plaintext and XSS-vulnerable.

entryPoints.label: Login (email + password)
entryPoints.description: User submits credentials to receive JWT token.

entryPoints.label: Page load (token recovery)
entryPoints.description: On page load, useAuth.tsx reads stored token and re-validates via GET /api/v1/auth/me.

exitPoints.label: Token cleared from storage (401 / logout)
exitPoints.description: Token removed from localStorage/sessionStorage and React state cleared.

preconditions: User has valid credentials in Supabase Auth
Frontend has access to browser storage APIs (localStorage, sessionStorage)
postconditions: After login: token stored in browser, attached to all subsequent API requests
After 401: token cleared, user redirected to login
After logout: all tokens cleared, Supabase session ended

loops.condition: Until token expires or user logs out

errorPaths.destination: apiClient.ts response interceptor clears token from storage, redirects to login
errorPaths.recovery: User must re-authenticate via login page. No automatic refresh.
Clear token, redirect to login, re-authenticate.

errorPaths.trigger: Supabase Auth API unreachable during verification
errorPaths.destination: Middleware cannot validate token → 500 or 401 depending on error handling
errorPaths.recovery: Retry on next request once Supabase is reachable

validationRules: Token must be present in Authorization header as 'Bearer <token>'
Token must be a valid JWT per Supabase Auth API
Server-side Supabase client configured with autoRefreshToken: false, persistSession: false
businessRules: Token stored in localStorage if 'Remember Me' is checked, sessionStorage otherwise
Same token reused for all API requests during session—no rotation
401 response always triggers token clear and redirect—no distinction between expired vs invalid
securityConsiderations: CRITICAL: Token in plaintext localStorage—XSS vulnerability
CRITICAL: No refresh token rotation—user logged out mid-session
No token blacklist/revocation—logout is client-side only
Token stored in 2 places (localStorage + sessionStorage) depending on Remember Me
Supabase onAuthStateChange listener syncs Supabase session to localStorage
No cross-tab sync—active sessions in other tabs not notified of logout
performanceConsiderations: Token verification via remote Supabase API (not local JWT decode)—~100-300ms per request
No caching of verification result—every request re-validates

annotations.text: CRITICAL GAP: No refresh token rotation implemented. User loses session mid-activity.
VULNERABILITY: Token in localStorage accessible to any JS execution on the same origin
Remote API call for every authenticated request—no local JWT decode
